title: Food Program Must Help Fewer Families in Gaza
summary:
The World Food Programme, or WFP, is part of the United Nations. It gives food to people who need it. Now it says it does not have enough money to help as many people in Gaza.

The WFP will help about 1.1 million people instead of 1.6 million. That is about a third fewer. Community kitchens will serve 150,000 hot meals a day instead of 250,000. Some families in hard-to-reach places will get a meal every other day instead of every day.

A WFP leader, Shaun Hughes, said the cuts are about money. He said people still need the food.

Most of Gaza's 2.1 million people have had to leave their homes. Two out of three people depend on food aid. Stores have food, but most people have no jobs and cannot buy it.

Parents are worried. One mother of five asked how she will feed her little ones. The cuts come as winter gets close.
why_it_matters: Just like kids everywhere, children in Gaza need enough food each day to stay healthy and learn.

keywords.explanation: The United Nations is a group of countries that work together to help people and keep peace.

Food aid is food given to people who cannot get enough on their own.
Cuts are reductions, which means making something smaller or giving less of it.

background_read: Gaza is a small Palestinian area by the sea where many families lost their homes after years of fighting.
The World Food Programme brings food to people in emergencies around the world.
It pays for that food with money that countries and others give, so when the money runs low, it can help fewer people.
